 More than 400 cases of locally acquired dengue have been reported this year in Florida , according to the Florida Department of Health's weekly arbovirus surveillance report.
 The report for the period from Oct. 18-24 says that "485 cases of locally acquired dengue and 20 mosquito pools have been reported from twelve counties" in 2026. From Oct. 18-24 alone, 60 cases of locally acquired dengue were reported in Florida.
 Hillsborough County saw 385 of the 485 reported dengue cases this year. Brevard County saw one case, Broward County saw one, Citrus County saw three, Manatee County saw two, Miami-Dade County saw nine, Orange County saw nine, Palm Beach County saw one, Pasco County saw four, Pinellas County saw 67, Polk County saw one and Seminole County saw two.
 Dengue is also known as dengue fever or breakbone fever, the latter due to the pain it can cause. It can present as "a flu-like illness with severe muscle aches and joint pain," along with fever and "sometimes" a rash, according to the Florida Department of Health in Miami-Dade County .
 Symptoms of dengue will appear within 14 days of being bitten by an infected mosquito. Dengue is not contagious, and is transmitted via the bite of an infected Aedes aegypti mosquito.
 How to best prevent mosquito-borne illnesses
 In June, Miami-Dade County encouraged residents to "take proactive steps" to prevent the spread of mosquito-borne illnesses, including "frequently checking for and eliminating any standing water." That's the best protection against "container-breeding mosquitoes," said a press release by the county , which are the "likeliest species to transmit the viruses that cause dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever," illnesses that are among those  most commonly transmitted by mosquitoes .
 Standing water usually accumulates after rainfall or irrigation in items like potted planters, saucers, outdoor toys, coolers and boat/car tarps, according to the release.
 "As little as one teaspoon or bottle cap of water standing for more than one week is enough for mosquitoes to breed and multiply," according to a flyer provided by the FDOH .
 As for individual protection, mosquito repellent can help prevent bites while outdoors, especially between "dusk and dawn," when mosquitoes are most active.
 The county also suggests:
 Covering entrances to one's home, including windows and doors, with mesh screens
 Wearing clothes with long sleeves and pant legs to "maximize skin protection"
 Regularly cleaning rain gutters to avoid water pooling within them
 Filling up indentations in one's lawn, air conditioner drain areas and tree holes
 Regularly replacing water in outdoor pet dishes and birdbaths
 Requesting a mosquito inspection via the  county’s online portal
